title: Pre-flight warns that a step is scheduled 'before target rises' when it is scheduled AFTER the rise time it prints
what_happened: Pre-Flight Validation listed three warnings of the form: 'New Target: "Cool Camera" scheduled at 14:45 before target rises at 11:44' (also for Unpark Mount and Slew to Target at 14:55). 14:45 and 14:55 are both AFTER 11:44, and the target card for the same target shows Rise 11:44 / Transit 17:49 / Set 23:47, i.e. the target is up at run time. The warning states the opposite of the data on the adjacent card.
expected: No warning at all for a step scheduled between rise and set. If the intent is 'before the NEXT rise', the message must name that time, not a rise that already happened.
repro: Set site 30N/82E, build Target(RA 00h,Dec +00) with Cool Camera/Unpark/Slew/Autofocus/Take Exposures, press Start at 14:45 local. Read the Simulation section of the Pre-Flight dialog.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-39.png (three warning lines) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-32.png (Rise 11:44, Transit 17:49, Set 23:47 for the same target)
where: Sequencer > Builder > Start > Pre-Flight Validation > Simulation
location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, but the dialog only renders the string. The comparison and the text live in SequenceTimeEstimator.findTimingConflicts, packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:786-798 (the 'before target rises at' literal is line 791); _formatTime at line 411 prints HH:mm only, which is why a rise on a different calendar day reads as one that already passed.
proposed_fix: Compare the scheduled instant against the rise/set interval that CONTAINS it; only warn when the step really falls outside the visibility window, and print the boundary that was violated.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Site 30N/82E, target 'New Target' RA 00h00m00s / Dec +00d00'36", Start pressed at 16:54 local. Pre-Flight > Simulation printed three warnings: 'New Target: "Cool Camera" scheduled at 16:54 before target rises at 11:36' plus the same for Dither (17:04) and Unpark Mount (17:05). All three times are AFTER the 11:36 it prints. I computed the true window independently from the app's own LST readout (LST 23:12 at 16:54 local): for RA 0h/Dec 0, rise is at LST 18h -> ~11:42 local and set at LST 6h -> ~23:42 local, so the target is genuinely above the horizon at run time and no conflict exists at all. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png.

title: Pre-flight dark-library check uses the camera default temperature (-10C), not the temperature the sequence's Cool Camera node will actually reach (15C)
what_happened: The sequence's Cool Camera node was set to Target Temperature 15C (confirmed on the node chip '15C' and in Properties). Pre-Flight's Dark Library section reported 'No matching darks found for 1 exposure combination: gain=100, offset=50, temp=-10.0C, duration=3s, binning=1x1'. During the run the camera reported Cam: 15.0C. The check therefore matched darks against a temperature the run never uses, and the 'Capture missing darks' action it offers would capture darks at the wrong temperature.
expected: Dark matching should use the setpoint the sequence will actually be at (the Cool Camera node value, 15C), or say which temperature it assumed and why.
repro: Add Cool Camera, set Target Temperature 15. Add Take Exposures 4x3s. Start -> read Pre-Flight > Dark Library.
where: Sequencer > Builder > Start > Pre-Flight Validation > Dark Library
location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart; the temperature is chosen in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart:116-118 ('final cameraState = ref.read(cameraStateProvider); final camTargetTemp = cameraState.targetTemp;') and stamped onto every DarkFrameRequirement at line 139. Nothing there consults the sequence's CoolCameraNode.
proposed_fix: Resolve the planned sensor temperature from the sequence's cooling instruction chain before querying the dark library; fall back to the camera default only when no Cool Camera node precedes the exposures.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. The sequence's Cool Camera node was set to Target Temperature 15 (node chip '15C', Properties field 15) and the run held 15.0C. Pre-Flight > Dark Library still reported 'No matching darks found for 1 exposure combination: gain=100, offset=50, temp=-10.0C, duration=3s, binning=1x1'. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png. Code confirms it is unconditional, not a race.

title: Four surfaces disagree about which filter a frame was taken through: filename says 'nofilter', DB says 'R', FITS header has no FILTER card, run stats say 'Unknown'
what_happened: For the same 4 frames of run 1: the files on disk are named 'New Target_nofilter_0001.fits'...'_0004.fits'; captured_images.filter = 'R' for all four; the FITS headers contain no FILTER keyword at all; the Session Report's Targets table shows Filter 'R'; and sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown buckets them under filter key 'Unknown'. The live telemetry strip during the run showed 'Filter: R'.
expected: One answer. If the wheel is on slot R, the filename, the FITS FILTER card, the DB column and the run stats all say R.
repro: Connect the simulated filter wheel, run a Take Exposures node with no explicit filter, then compare ls of the capture folder, the FITS header, captured_images.filter, and stats_json.targetBreakdown.
evidence: ls /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/captures/ ; FITS header dump (no FILTER card); sqlite captured_images.filter='R'; sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown {"New Sequence":{"Unknown":{...}}}; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png (Session Report shows Filter R)
where: Sequencer run -> file naming / FITS writer / captured_images / run stats
location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_report_dialog.dart' - that dialog is one of five disagreeing readers and decides none of it. Writers: the Rust FITS/filename writer (no FILTER card, 'nofilter' token), event_operations.dart (~line 625: filter = progress.currentFilter ?? filterWheelStateProvider.currentFilterName), and whatever builds sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown.
proposed_fix: Resolve the filter name once at exposure start and thread that single value into the filename template, the FITS FILTER card, the DB column and the stats bucket.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own run (Target > Take Exposures 4x3s, node Filter empty - 'No filters in profile' - sim wheel parked on slot R). All five surfaces verified independently: (1) files on disk 'New Target_nofilter_0001..0004.fits'; (2) captured_images.filter = 'R' on all four rows; (3) the FITS header of _0001 has 27 cards and no FILTER card (dumped byte-wise, not via the app); (4) sequence_runs.stats_json = {"targetBreakdown":{"New Sequence":{"Unknown":{"captured":4,...}}}}; (5) the Session Report Targets table shows Filter 'R' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-18.png). Two extras the finding missed: the same targetBreakdown keys the TARGET as 'New Sequence' (the sequence name) not 'New Target', and the Session Report labels the group 'Untargeted' - the breakdown is wrong on both axes. Severity corrected to P2: the frames really are taken through whatever slot the wheel sits on and the run is undamaged; the harm is downstream attribution ambiguity.

title: Session report says 'Autofocus 0' after an autofocus that ran 9 points and completed successfully
what_happened: Run 1 executed the Autofocus node: the live tree showed 'Autofocus - Point 5 of 9', the log shows 'Autofocus point 9 sample 1/1 completed' and "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success", and the focuser moved from 25000 to 25074. The Session Report's Mount/Focus block shows Autofocus '0', and sequence_runs.stats_json has "autofocusRuns":0. focus_models is also empty (0 rows).
expected: autofocusRuns == 1, and the report should show the resulting focus position / HFR so the user can tell whether focus was achieved.
repro: Add an Autofocus node to a sequence, run it, open the Session Report and read the Autofocus counter; compare with app.log 'completed with status: Success'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png (Autofocus 0); /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log 18:47:36 "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success"; stats_json autofocusRuns:0; focuser 25000 -> 25074
where: Sequencer > Session Report > Mount & focus block; sequence_runs.stats_json
proposed_fix: Increment the autofocus counter where the AutofocusNode reports Success, not where the (unused) focus-model persistence path runs.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Run 2 executed the Autofocus node: app.log shows 'Autofocus point 1..9 sample 1/1 completed' and "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success" at 21:01:46Z, and the focuser moved 25000 -> 25070. The Session Report's Mount / operations block reads 'Autofocus runs 0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png), sequence_runs id=2 stats_json has autofocusRuns:0, imaging_sessions.autofocus_count is 0, and focus_models has 0 rows. Root cause is total and mechanical: SequenceRunStats.recordAutofocus() (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:160) has ZERO non-test call sites - grep for 'recordAutofocus()' returns only the definition - so the counter can never be anything but 0. recordTriggerFire and recordMeridianFlip, by contrast, are wired up at event_operations.dart:317 and :926.

title: Frames captured under a named target are reported as 'Untargeted', and the run's target breakdown is keyed by the SEQUENCE name instead of the target name
what_happened: The sequence had exactly one Target node called 'New Target' and every exposure ran underneath it (the FITS OBJECT card and the filenames both say 'New Target'). The Session Report's Targets section shows a single group titled 'Untargeted - 4/4 frames | 12s'. sequence_runs.stats_json targetBreakdown is {"New Sequence": {"Unknown": {...}}} - keyed by the sequence's name, not the target's. captured_images.target_id is NULL for all 4 rows.
expected: 'New Target - 4/4 frames', targetBreakdown keyed 'New Target', and captured_images.target_id pointing at that target.
repro: Build Target 'New Target' with Take Exposures under it, run, open the Session Report and read the Targets section; then read stats_json.targetBreakdown.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-44.png ('Untargeted 4/4 frames'); stats_json targetBreakdown {"New Sequence":{"Unknown":...}}; captured_images.target_id NULL x4
proposed_fix: Attribute each frame to the enclosing TargetHeaderNode (the executor already knows it - the filename template resolves the target name) and persist the target id on the captured_images row.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Sequence 'New Sequence' with one Target node named 'New Target'; all 4 lights ran under it. Session Report > Targets shows a single group 'Untargeted  4/4 frames | 1m 20s' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png). sequence_runs id=2 stats_json targetBreakdown is {"New Sequence": {"Unknown": {captured:4,...}}} - keyed by the SEQUENCE name, filter 'Unknown' even though captured_images.filter is 'R'. captured_images.target_id is empty for all 4 rows and the targets table has 0 rows. The keying is the documented fallback chain at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:877-883: target = progress.currentTarget ?? currentSequenceProvider.name ?? 'Sequence', i.e. currentTarget was never populated (no TargetStarted/TargetChanged consumed) so it fell through to the sequence name.

title: The top-bar run chip still reads 'Sequence Running' (green) while the sequence is paused
what_happened: With run 2 paused at 3/4 exposures (toolbar chip 'Paused 75%', node badge 'PAUSED', Pause button flipped to Resume, and no further frames being captured), the chip in the Sequencer's top tab bar - the app's most prominent run indicator - still showed a green dot and the text 'Sequence Running'. The accessibility tree confirms both strings are present simultaneously: 'panel: Sequence Running' and 'panel: Paused 75%'.
expected: The top-bar chip should read Paused (amber) when the run is paused. Two indicators one row apart must not disagree about whether the rig is exposing.
repro: Start a sequence, wait for exposures, click Pause, read the chip next to the Builder/Templates/Sequences/History tabs and compare with the toolbar chip.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-50.png (green 'Sequence Running' chip while paused); tree output showing 'Sequence Running', 'Paused 75%', 'PAUSED' at the same instant
where: Sequencer > top tab bar run chip
proposed_fix: Drive the chip from the same run-state enum as the toolbar chip instead of a boolean isRunning.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Run 3 paused at 17:06:37 mid-exposure. At 17:06:41 the accessibility tree simultaneously carried 'PAUSED' (node badge), 'panel: Sequence Running', 'Paused 25%' (toolbar chip) and a 'Resume' button; 45 seconds later progress was still frozen at 2/4 with 'Paused 50%'. The cropped capture of the Sequencer tab row (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/40.png) shows the chip rendered with a GREEN dot and the literal text 'Sequence Running' at that moment. The finding's location is correct: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/sequencer_screen_parts/tab_bar.dart:112 hard-codes 'Sequence Running' with colors.success and there is no paused variant.

title: sequence_runs.status stays 'running' while the run is paused, so any non-GUI consumer thinks the rig is still exposing
what_happened: During a 52-second pause of run 2 the DB row kept status='running'. The GUI knew it was paused, but the persisted state (which the headless API, the web dashboard and the mobile client read) did not distinguish paused from running.
expected: A 'paused' status (or a paused_at column) so remote surfaces can show the true state.
repro: Pause a run, then: sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select status from sequence_runs where id=2;"
evidence: status='running' at 18:55:36 (paused) and still 'running' at 18:56:28, while the GUI showed PAUSED throughout
proposed_fix: Persist the paused state on pause and clear it on resume.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and additionally proven from the schema. Run 3 paused at 17:06:37; sqlite3 on /tmp/ns-audit/v2-sequencer-run/data/skotiq.db returned status='running' for id=3 at 17:06:41 and still 'running' at 17:06:59, while the GUI showed PAUSED / 'Paused 50%' / Resume and frame progress was frozen. The table cannot express the state: .schema sequence_runs is (id, sequence_id, sequence_name, started_at, ended_at, status TEXT DEFAULT 'running', stats_json, sequence_snapshot_json) - no paused_at column, and 'paused' is never written mid-run (a terminal 'paused-stopped' is written only after Stop).
severity_note: P2 (raised from P3) - this is the same single defect as the P2 top-bar-chip finding (no paused state is modelled anywhere), and this is the half that reaches unattended remote operators who have no GUI to correct them.

title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header and with a real profile active
what_happened: Relaunching the app after a night's session shows the Continue Session dialog titled 'New Sequence', with the rows 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile' and 'Sequence: No Sequence', above a primary button 'Load Previous Setup'. The scratch DB has exactly one equipment profile named 'My Equipment' (which the status bar shows as active) and one sequence named 'New Sequence' (which the dialog's own header prints, and which the dashboard card behind it names too). Both fields the dialog needs to restore are unresolved nulls: quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 falls back to 'Unknown Profile'/'No Sequence' when quickStartContext.profileName/sequenceName are null.
expected: 'Equipment Profile: My Equipment', 'Sequence: New Sequence'. This is the dialog whose whole purpose is telling you what it is about to restore; if it cannot name it, the user cannot trust the button.
repro: Run a sequence, quit the app, relaunch on the same profile. Read the Continue Session dialog.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-60.png; sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> 1|My Equipment; sequence_runs row 2 named 'New Sequence'
where: App launch > Continue Session (quick start / session handoff) dialog
location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart. The dialog that shows this is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart (the finding's own body names it correctly); session_handoff_dialog.dart exists but is a different surface.
proposed_fix: Populate quickStartContext.profileName/sequenceName from the persisted last-run row (sequence_runs.sequence_name and the active profile) instead of from in-memory state that is empty on a cold start.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on relaunch. Dialog titled 'Continue Session', card header prints 'New Sequence', and directly beneath it 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile' and 'Sequence: No Sequence' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png). The DB has exactly one equipment profile, 'My Equipment', which the status bar shows as active. The cited file:line is correct - quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 reads 'profileName ?? \'Unknown Profile\'' and 'sequenceName ?? \'No Sequence\''. I also found the upstream cause the finding did not: the run's own imaging_sessions rows are written with profile_id NULL and sequence_id NULL (select id,profile_id,sequence_id from imaging_sessions -> 1||, 2||, 3||), and QuickStartService builds the context from imaging_sessions (quick_start_service.dart:624). Changing the fallback string alone would not fix it.

title: Continue Session dialog dates yesterday's session as 'Today at 14:57'
what_happened: Relaunched the app on 2026-08-02 at 10:40 local. The Continue Session dialog header reads 'Today at 14:57'. The session it refers to is sequence_runs id=2, ended_at=1785610650 = Sat Aug 1 14:57:30 EDT - i.e. YESTERDAY. The dashboard card behind the same dialog gets it right ('Completed - 19 hours ago') and the app's own date header says 'Sun Aug 2'. So two surfaces one dialog apart disagree about which day the run happened, and the modal one is wrong.
expected: 'Yesterday at 14:57' (or the date). A handoff dialog exists to tell you whether the state it is about to restore is from the night you are still in; getting the day wrong defeats its only job.
repro: Run a sequence, quit, relaunch the app the next calendar day, read the Continue Session dialog header.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-71.png ('Continue Session / Today at 14:57' over a card reading 'Completed - 19 hours ago'); sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select ended_at from sequence_runs where id=2' -> 1785610650 -> Sat Aug 1 14:57:30 EDT 2026; system date Sun Aug 2 10:40
where: App launch > Continue Session dialog header
location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart; the code is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116. The finding's repro also attributes the timestamp to sequence_runs.ended_at - it is not: I shifted sequence_runs by 19h and the header did not move at all. The date comes from imaging_sessions.end_time via QuickStartService (quick_start_service.dart:624).
proposed_fix: Format the timestamp with a calendar-day comparison (today / yesterday / explicit date) instead of assuming the last session is from the current day.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced deliberately. I backdated the audit profile's imaging_sessions rows by 19 hours (last session end_time -> 2026-08-02 22:03:07 local, i.e. YESTERDAY) and relaunched at 2026-08-03 17:10. The dialog header printed 'Continue Session / Today at 22:03' while the dashboard card one layer behind it correctly read 'Paused-stopped - 19 hours ago' and the briefing header said 'Mon Aug 3' - all three visible in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png. The bug is unconditional in quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116: _formatDate compares ELAPSED time ('final diff = now.difference(dt); if (diff.inDays == 0) return \'Today at ...\''), so any session under 24h old is labelled Today regardless of calendar day, and 'Yesterday' can only ever appear for sessions 24-48h old.

title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and writes nothing to the log - it just closes the dialog
what_happened: On relaunch I clicked the Continue Session dialog's primary button 'Load Previous Setup' (the only styled action; 'Skip' is the secondary). The dialog closed and NOTHING else changed: the status bar still read Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected / Focus ---, the profile chip still read 'My Equipment 0/0', the Sequencer builder still held an empty 'New Sequence' with '0 targets / Sequence 0 steps', and app.log recorded not one line between the click at 10:41:30 and 10:42:40 (no connect attempt, no sequence load, no error). The previous session had 4 connected simulators and a 5-node sequence.
expected: Either it reconnects the previous equipment and loads the previous sequence, or - if it cannot resolve them, which it already admits by printing 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' - the button is disabled with an explanation. A primary action that silently no-ops is worse than no button: after a crash mid-night this is the control a user reaches for first.
repro: Run a sequence with simulators connected, quit the app, relaunch, click 'Load Previous Setup', then read the status bar, the profile chip and the Sequencer builder.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-71.png (dialog); tree after the click shows 'Camera Disconnected', 'Mount Disconnected', 'My Equipment 0/0', 'New Sequence / 0 targets / Sequence 0 steps'; /tmp/ns-audit/r-sequencer-run/app.log has zero entries in the 70s following the click
where: App launch > Continue Session > Load Previous Setup
location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart'. The dialog is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart ('Load Previous Setup' label at line 407) and the behaviour is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_checker.dart:_handleStartFresh (~line 244). session_handoff_service.dart is a different feature (cross-device carry-over).
proposed_fix: Wire the button to the same restore path the profile auto-connect uses, and gate it on the context actually resolving (same nulls that produce 'Unknown Profile'/'No Sequence' should disable it).
verdict_reasoning: The no-op is real; the 'silent' half is not, and the truth is worse. Four completed runs with 4 sims connected, quit, relaunch: the 'Continue Session' dialog appears with 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile / Sequence: No Sequence / Progress 4/4 frames captured' and 'Load Previous Setup' as primary (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-42.png). Clicking it restores nothing - status bar still Camera/Mount/Guider Disconnected, Focus '---', profile chip 'My Equipment 0/0'. But it is NOT silent: a full-width green success snackbar reads 'Loaded previous setup for previous target from frame 1' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-43.png and the same string in the a11y tree). So this is a false-success claim, not a dead button - cry-wolf class, and it changes the fix. The finding's log evidence proves nothing: app.log is the Rust tracing stream only and contains no Dart-side lines at all (zero 'QuickStart'/'SequenceExecutor'/'ImagesDao' sources in 904 lines of mine or in the original agent's), so the Dart logger's 'Starting fresh with context:' line could never appear there. Mechanism: _handleStartFresh only acts when context.profileId / context.sequenceId are non-null plus the equipment snapshot; all four of my imaging_sessions rows have profile_id NULL, sequence_id NULL and empty equipment_snapshot, so there is genuinely nothing to restore - the dialog already says so and then offers the action anyway and reports success. Fixes: disable/relabel the primary when the snapshot is empty, and/or stamp profile_id/sequence_id/equipment_snapshot onto imaging_sessions. P2: no data lost, the damage is the false claim.

title: Builder and Pre-Flight disagree about how long the same sequence takes: '~18m 54s' vs 'Duration 27m'
what_happened: The identical 7-step sequence (Cool 15C, Slew, Autofocus, 4x3s lights, Unpark, Park, Warm 20C @2C/min) is estimated at '~18m 54s' by the estimate chip in the Builder header and at 'Duration 27m / Ends 11:20' by the Pre-Flight Simulation panel, both visible in the same screenshot with the dialog open over the builder. That is a 43% disagreement. The header estimate also did not move at all when I changed the Cool Camera setpoint from -10C to +15C (ambient 20C), i.e. after removing ~25C of cooling work the builder still printed exactly ~18m 54s.
expected: One estimate, computed once. Session planning (will this finish before dawn?) depends on it, and the pre-flight's 'Ends 11:20' is what a user schedules around.
repro: Builder: add Cool Camera / Slew / Autofocus / Take Exposures 4x3s / Unpark / Park / Warm Camera. Read the estimate chip next to the sequence header. Press Start and read Simulation > Duration.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-84.png - builder chip '~18m 54s' at the top right of the tree, dialog panel 'Duration 27m', 'Ends 11:20', taken 10:53:40
where: Sequencer > Builder header estimate vs Start > Pre-Flight > Simulation
location_wrong: unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, which is only one of the two disagreeing sides. The Builder chip/timeline uses SequenceTimeEstimator (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart, called from screens/sequencer/widgets/node_timing_section.dart:119-128 and sequence_timeline.dart:55-65); the Pre-Flight panel uses PreSessionSimulator().simulate(...) (preflight_validation_dialog.dart:134, rendered at :735). Two engines, not one dialog.
proposed_fix: Have both surfaces call the same estimator; if the pre-flight adds slew/settle/overheads the builder does not, show the same breakdown in both instead of two bare numbers.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own sequence (Target > Cool Camera 15C, Dither, Unpark, Slew, Autofocus, Take Exposures 4x3s). In one frame (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png): Builder header estimate chip '~14m 9s'; Pre-Flight > Simulation 'Duration 12m' and 'Ends 17:07' against a 16:54 start (= 13m implied). Three different numbers for the same sequence. Note also the Cool Camera Properties panel shows 'Max cooling time 10m / Duration: 10m / Contributes 29.3% of total', i.e. the Builder bills the node's Max Duration, which makes the finding's secondary claim (estimate does not move when the setpoint changes) plausible - I did not isolate that sub-claim.
severity_note: P2 (unchanged) - but the magnitude I measured is ~18%, not the 43% claimed; the disagreement itself is real and simultaneous on one screen.
